office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: An open seat left by Rep. Jeremie Dufault, who is running for the Senate. Republican Reedy Berg, Yakima's deputy mayor and a middle-school teacher, led the primary with 48%; attorney Liz Hallock, running under a "No Kings" party preference, advanced with 30%.

candidates.summary: Yakima deputy mayor and Toppenish middle-school history teacher running on lower taxes, Climate Commitment Act repeal and parental rights.
highlights: Opposes the state's new income tax and proposes a 0.1% sales-tax cut [S2]
Would repeal the Climate Commitment Act [S2]
Makes parents' right to know what children are taught and what medical decisions are made his first plank [S2]
On the city council, voted against sending a property-tax levy to voters and against a Pride Month proclamation [S6][S7]

taxes.basis: Opposes the income tax and new fees and taxes, proposes a sales-tax cut, and voted against placing a city property-tax levy on the ballot.

spending.basis: Pledges to cut wasteful spending and administrative overhead; says he would have cut more rather than use one-time money on city facilities.

housing.basis: Supports permitting reform to lower housing costs and says the Housing First model is not working.

safety.basis: Backs fully funding police, opposes criminal-justice rollbacks, and would require treatment as a condition of housing assistance.

climate.basis: Would repeal the Climate Commitment Act and reduce fuel taxes and regulations on energy production.

experience.basis: Two years on the Yakima City Council and now deputy mayor, while also presenting himself as 'not a career politician'.

social.basis: Voted against a Pride Month proclamation, stating there are two genders and that science does not support expanding gender identities.

parental-rights.basis: Platform says parents have the right to know what children are taught and what medical decisions are made, and that government has overstepped.

candidates.summary: Yakima family and public-disclosure attorney and repeat candidate, running under a "No Kings" party preference on economic inequality, reproductive rights and opposition to President Trump.
highlights: Ran in 2022 to "protect abortion rights and safe abortion access" [S4]
Says Christian teachings are being used "to terrorize immigrants" [S1]
Wants to protect Yakima residents "from the King in the White House" [S1]

social.basis: Says reproductive rights are being gutted; ran in 2022 on protecting abortion rights and access.

immigration.basis: Objects to immigrants being terrorized; no specific enforcement policy stated.

climate.basis: Says the environment and children's futures are being destroyed; worked with Citizens' Climate Lobby (2020).

experience.basis: Has not held government office; runs outside both major parties under a No Kings label.
